before.notes: State laws the screening engine applies here: CA SB 9 (California HOME Act) — two units per lot and urban lot split, CA: ADU and junior ADU approved ministerially on single-family lots. Unverified screening — confirm with the planning department.
panel_lines: • Geologic hazard zone — In state liquefaction hazard zone: new additions or ADUs require a site-specific geotechnical/soils investigation.
• Detached ADU (backyard home) — Building footprint is not on file, so open yard space cannot be verified without a site plan or survey.

✓ Junior ADU (inside the house, up to 500 sq ft) — 4,088 sq ft single-family home: state law (Gov. Code §§ 66313 and 66333) allows converting up to 500 sq ft of interior livable space; under the current text of § 66333, owner-occupancy can be required only if the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the house, and rentals must be longer than 30 days.

? SB 9 lot split / second home — 2,870 sq ft parcel: in a single-family zone, SB 9 allows a split into two lots of roughly equal area, each at least 1,200 sq ft and at least 40% of the original (about 1,435 sq ft each here), if the lot meets the law's other conditions, which aren't checked here (among them: the split can't require demolishing or altering housing occupied by a tenant in the last three years or under rent control or an affordability covenant, and the parcel must meet the site conditions of Gov. Code § 65913.4(a)(6)(B)–(K) as it read on 16 Sep 2021). A city doesn't have to allow more than two units on each new lot (Gov. Code § 66411.7(j)).
May apply: CA SB 9 (California HOME Act) — two units per lot and urban lot split, CA: ADU and junior ADU approved ministerially on single-family lots
Private covenants: state housing laws override city zoning but may not cancel recorded HOA covenants or CC&Rs. Check the title report.
Garage to living space (not an ADU)
